title: Inventory went negative
summary: Repair a stock check that accepts impossible orders.

scenario.briefing: An order for zero notebooks slipped through, and a negative quantity pushed stock above its real value. Repair canFulfill so it accepts only whole quantities from 1 through available stock.

objectives.description: Reject zero, negative, fractional, and over-stock quantities.
Preserve valid orders at and below the stock limit.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: A valid quantity has a lower bound as well as an upper bound.
Reject when quantity is less than 1 or greater than stock.
Also reject non-integers and negative stock, because neither describes a real shipment.
Return false unless Number.isInteger(stock) && Number.isInteger(quantity) && stock >= 0 && quantity >= 1 && quantity <= stock.

misconceptions.feedback: The upper bound alone accepts zero and negative quantities. A valid shipment also needs a lower bound.
An order of 1.5 notebooks is not a whole item. Reject non-integer quantities unless the product explicitly supports fractions.

sections.title: Conditions need both edges
sections.body: A range check has a lower and an upper boundary. quantity <= stock silently accepts 0 and negative numbers because they are small. A complete rule is quantity >= 1 and quantity <= stock, with type and integer checks where those values must be whole.

sections.title: Boundary tests find the gaps
sections.body: Test at the smallest valid value, the largest valid value, and one step outside each. Those cases reveal off-by-one errors and missing lower bounds far more reliably than a single ordinary example.

vocabulary.definition: A value at or just outside a valid limit.
A function that returns true or false.
A condition that enforces both a minimum and a maximum.

steps.title: Why both bounds matter

statements.label: A lower bound is needed to reject zero and negative quantities.
An upper bound alone accepts some impossible orders.
A condition that compiles must be logically correct.
Testing exact boundary values reveals counting mistakes.

steps.explanation: Compilation checks syntax, not intent. Both bounds and boundary tests are required for a range rule.
